 ‘Dead’ woman shows up at MP hearing, rues denial of pension, PDS 
 Trending Karnataka Bus Fare Rise Delhi Murder Bombay High Court Pune techie suicide Patanjali Ghee Mahadev Betting App Karnataka Bus Fare Rise Delhi Murder Bombay High Court Pune techie suicide Patanjali Ghee Mahadev Betting App Karnataka Bus Fare Rise Delhi Murder Bombay High Court Pune techie suicide Patanjali Ghee Mahadev Betting App ‘Dead’ woman shows up at MP hearing, rues denial of pension, PDS 
 Karishma.Kotwal / Nov 04, 2026, 00:33 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Indore: Declared dead in official records and without pension and ration for three years, an elderly woman, with no fingers and impaired vision, showed up at a public hearing (jan sunwai) on Tuesday in Madhya Pradesh’s Khandwa district to prove she was alive. In heartbreaking scenes as the others watched, the woman narrated how she fell out of the state’s public distribution system and pension coverage, as she couldn’t authenticate her identity through fingerprints or an iris scan. Battling leprosy, the woman said she was forced to make the rounds of govt offices from Nirmal Dham Kushth Ashram where she resides, just to prove she wasn’t dead as shown in govt records. She said her daily-wager husband struggled to meet daily expenses and put meals on the table for three years, while she was denied the benefits she was entitled to due to a clerical error or mistaken entry into the official records. As she shared her plight at Tuesday’s hearing, officials admitted that her death had been wrongly recorded in her Samagra ID. After making numerous rounds of govt offices over three turbulent years, presenting herself as proof of life, the elderly was finally assured that the mistaken entry would be corrected within a day or two and her pension and ration would be restored. Samagra is the official digital database of the Madhya Pradesh govt for channeling and extending all promised welfare benefits to citizens. The woman was unable to complete her Aadhaar application as she could neither provide fingerprints nor do an iris scan, as is mandated by UIDAI , the statutory nodal authority for all Aadhaar applications and enrolments. However, instead of exploring an alternative mechanism to process her Aadhaar enrolment, she was shown as ‘dead’ in Samagra record. The administrative error led to a halt in her pension payments, while also depriving her of ration for three years. Arriving at the public hearing convened by the district collector, the elderly alleged she was turned away from govt offices and treated with disdain as she tried to get the error corrected. She urged restoration of her pension and ration benefits at the earliest, while also demanding strict action against erring officials. Zila Panchayat CEO Aishwarya Verma said the village administration had sought a report on receipt of the woman’s application, confirming that her record was erased from the Samagra portal as she couldn’t complete her fingerprint and iris scan. “As soon as we came to know about her grievance, we put together a team to investigate the matter. A ticket has been raised in her name and an update of her Aadhaar details has been sought. By tomorrow (Wednesday), her Aadhaar details will be updated. We are checking how long she hasn’t been receiving pension. The benefits will be restored soon,” Verma said.
